x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His saying Ya Seen.
Some of them said: It is an oath by which God swore, and it is one of the names of God.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Ya Seen, he said: It is an oath that God swore, and it is one of the names of God.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: O man.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, he said: Al-Hasan bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement Ya Seen, he said: O human being in Abyssinian.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Sharqi, who said:
m: I heard ʿIkrimah say: The interpretation of Ya-Seen is: O human being.

x: Others said: It is the key to the words with which God opened His words.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Ya Seen is the key to speech, God began His speech with it.

x: Others said: Rather, it is one of the names of the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazi told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Ya Seen, he said: Every satire in the Qur’an is a name of the Qur’an.

x: We have already explained the statement in the past regarding similar letters of the alphabet, so there is no need to repeat it here.
And his saying, And the Wise Qur’an, means: And the decisive Qur’an with what it contains of its rulings and clear proofs.

You are indeed one of the messengers. God Almighty says, swearing by His revelation and sending down to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You, O Muhammad, are indeed one of the messengers by God's revelation to His servants.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “And the Wise Qur’an. Indeed, you are among the messengers.” An oath as you hear: “Indeed, you are among the messengers. On a straight path.”

x: And his saying,
h
On a straight path
, means: On a path of guidance without any crookedness, which is Islam.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
On a straight path
: meaning on Islam. As for His statement,
h
on a straight path

, there are two interpretations: One of them is that its meaning is: Indeed, you are among the messengers on the straight path of truth. In that case, upon is the relative clause of sending. The other is that it is a predicate of the subject, as if it was said: Indeed, you are among the messengers, indeed, you are
h
on a straight path

x: The reciters differed in reading the statement the revelation of the Almighty, the Most Merciful. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it the revelation of the Almighty with the nominative case of the revelation. The nominative case in this case is directed in two ways: One of them: by making it a predicate, so the meaning of the statement is: it is a revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful. The other: by starting, so the meaning of the statement in this case is: you are indeed among the messengers, this is a revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Ash-Sham read it as the revelation in the accusative case as a source of the statement you are indeed among the messengers, because sending is only from the revelation, so it is as if it was said: for the one who sent down the revelation of the Almighty, the Most Merciful, truly.

The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. The meaning of the statement is: Indeed, you are one of the messengers, O Muhammad, sent by the Almighty Lord to take revenge on the disbelievers in Him, the Most Merciful to those who repent to Him and turn back from their disbelief and immorality, to punish them for their previous crime after their repentance to Him.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement,
h
To warn a people whose fathers were not warned
Some of them said: Its meaning is:
h
To warn a people whose fathers were not warned
before them.
Mention of who said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us:

c: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of ʿIkrimah,
m: regarding this verse,
h
To warn a people whose fathers were not warned
, he said: They were warned.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is
h
to warn a people whose fathers were not warned
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned.

x: Some of them said: That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, from the warning of the people before them. And some of them said: That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned: that is, this nation to whom no warner came, until Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of ma in the phrase ma anthdhartuhu abahhum if the meaning of the statement is directed to the fact that their fathers had been warned, and it does not mean denial.

Some of the Basran grammarians said: The meaning of that, if it is not meant to mean denial, is: To warn them of the One who warned their fathers, so they are heedless. He said: The use of the letter fa in this meaning is not permissible, and God knows best. He said: It is better to deny it, so the meaning of the statement is: Indeed, you are among the messengers to a people whose fathers were warned, because they were in the interval.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: If ma does not mean denial, then the meaning of the statement is: To warn them of what their fathers were warned of. So the preposition ba is thrown in, and ma is in the accusative case. They are heedless. He says: They are heedless of what God will do to His enemies who associate others with Him, of bringing down His vengeance and His power upon them.
And His statement,
h
The word has come true upon most of them

, so they do not believe. God Almighty says: Punishment has become obligatory upon most of them, because God has decreed upon them in the Mother of the Book that they will not believe in God, nor will they believe in His Messenger.

God Almighty says: Indeed, We have made the oaths of these disbelievers chained to their necks with shackles, so that they will not be extended with any good, and it is in the reading of Abdullah in what he mentioned Indeed, We have placed shackles on their right hands, so they are up to the chins and his saying up to the chins means: So their right hands are bound with the shackles on their necks, so it is a metaphor for the oaths, and it was not mentioned to the listeners to know the meaning of the speech, and that if the shackles were on the necks, they would not be except with the hands of the shackled ones bound to them, so mentioning the shackles being on the necks dispensed with mentioning the oaths, as the poet said: I do not know, if I set my face intending good, which of the two will be more suitable for me. Is it for the good that I seek, or the evil that does not come to me? So he referred to evil, but he only mentioned good because the listener would know the meaning of the speaker, since evil is mentioned along with good.

Chins: plural of chin, and chin: the meeting of the two beards. His saying, They are covered with humpbacked hair. Al-Muqamih means someone who lowers his chin until it reaches the chest, then raises his head, according to some scholars of Arabic language from Basra. According to some Kufians, it means someone who lowers his gaze after raising his head. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, We have placed shackles on their necks, reaching to their chins, so their heads are raised, he said: It is like the statement of God, And do not make your hand chained to your neck (al-Isra’ 17:29), meaning by that that their hands are chained to their necks, and they are unable to extend them for good.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They will be with their heads up, he said: They will be raising their heads and placing their hands over their mouths.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, We have placed shackles on their necks, reaching to their chins, so their heads are covered with humps. That is, they are chained and prevented from all good. And His statement, And We placed before them a barrier, means, the Most High says, And We placed before these polytheists a barrier, which is a partition between two things. If it is pronounced with a fatha, it is from the actions of the children of Adam, and if it is from the actions of God, it is with a damma. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it with a damma.

x: Some of the Meccans and the majority of the Kufic reciters read it with a fatha on the seen as sada in both letters. The damma is the reading that I like the most in this regard, even though the other is permissible and correct.

x: What he meant by his saying,
h
And We placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier

, is that He made their evil deeds seem good to them, so they are blind, do not see what is right, and do not truly pay attention. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

m: regarding his statement,

m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier from the truth, so they hesitate.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier
. He said: Misguidance.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them so they do not see, he said: This has been placed as a barrier between them and Islam and faith, so they cannot reach it. And he recited, And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe, and he recited, Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe

(Yunus 10:96)
... the entire verse. And he said: Whoever God has prevented, he cannot. His statement,
h
So We covered them
, so they do not see, means: So We covered the eyes of these people, meaning We put a veil over them, so they do not see guidance nor benefit from it.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So We covered them

so they do not see guidance, nor do they benefit from it. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Abu Jahl bin Hisham when he swore that he would kill him or smash his head with a rock. The narration mentioned that:

c: Imran bin Musa told me: Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us: Ammarah bin Abi Hafsah told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Abu Jahl said:
m: If I see Muhammad, I will do this and that. Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, We have placed shackles around their necks… until His saying: so they do not see. He said: So they would say: This is Muhammad. He would say: Where is he, where is he? He would not see him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to read it So We blinded them, so they do not see with the letter ‘ayn, meaning We blinded them from it. This is because blindness means walking at night and not seeing.

evidence.text: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read it So We blinded them, so they do not see with the letter ‘ayn, meaning We blinded them from it.

x: God Almighty says: It is the same, O Muhammad, for those upon whom the word has come into effect, whether you warn them or leave them out, for they will not believe, because God has judged them to that.
And His statement,
h
You can only warn him who follows the message

, God Almighty says: Your warning, O Muhammad, only benefits him who believes in the Qur'an and follows what is in it of God's rulings. And fears the Most Merciful, meaning: and fears God when he is absent from the sight of onlookers, not the hypocrite who belittles God's religion when he is alone and shows faith in public, nor the polytheist whose heart God has sealed. And His statement,
h
Then give him good tidings of forgiveness

, meaning: So give good tidings, O Muhammad, to this one who followed the message and feared the Most Merciful in private, of forgiveness from God for his sins. And a noble reward, meaning: and a noble reward from Him for him in the Hereafter, and that is that He will give him Paradise for that deed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: You only warn those who follow the message. Following the message means following the Qur’an.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life of those We created and record what they have put forth in this world of good and evil, righteous and bad deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth of deeds.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And We record what they have put forth
, he said: what they did.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, what they have sent forth, he said: their deeds. His statement, and their traces, means: and the traces of their footsteps. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about a people who wanted to approach the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that he would approach them.

x: Who said that?

c: Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The homes of the Ansar were far from the mosque, so they wanted to move to the mosque, so the verse
h
And We record what they have put forth
and their traces was revealed. They said: We will remain in our place.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The Ansar lived far from the mosque, so they wanted to move. He said: Then the verse
h
And We record what they have put forth
and what they left behind was revealed, so they remained steadfast.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us: Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: The Banu Salamah wanted to go near the mosque. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: O Banu Salamah, your homes are where your traces are recorded.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Mu’tamir told us:
m: I heard Kahmas narrating, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Banu Salamah wanted to move closer to the mosque, and the places were empty. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Banu Salamah, your homes are recording your traces. So they stayed and said: It would not please us if we had moved.”

c: Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Tarif, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said:
m: “Banu Salamah complained to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the distance between their homes, so the verse, ‘Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life,
h
and We record what they have put forth
and what they left behind.’” He said: Your homes are yours, and your left behind will be recorded.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Abu Tamila told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Thabit:
m: “I walked on the authority of Anas, and I walked quickly. He took my hand, and we walked slowly. When we finished the prayer, Anas said: I walked with Zaid ibn Thabit, and I walked quickly. He said: O Anas, do you not realize that the reports are written down?”

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: that the homes of Banu Salamah were far from the mosque, so they decided to move closer to the mosque and attend the prayer with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Do you not consider your footsteps, O Banu Salamah? So they stayed in their homes.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Surat Yasin: 12 Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life,
h
and We record what they have put forth
and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register. What they have put forth and their traces, he said: Their footsteps with their feet.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And their traces, he said: their footsteps.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And their traces. He said: Al-Hasan said: And their traces. He said: Their steps. Qatada said: If he had been unaware of anything about you, O son of Adam, he would have been unaware of what the winds erase of these traces. And His statement,
h
And We have recorded everything in a clear register

, God Almighty says: And everything that was or will be, We have recorded it and established it in the Mother of the Book, which is the clear register. And it was said, clear, because it explains the truth of everything that is established in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: In a clear Imam, he said: In the Mother of the Book.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,

, everything is recorded with God in a book.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,

, he said: The Mother of the Book, in which are all things, is the clear register.

x: God Almighty says: And, O Muhammad, give an example to the polytheists of your al-Nas 114:the people of the town. He mentioned that it was Antioch. When there came to it the messengers.
The scholars differed regarding these messengers and who sent them to the people of the town.
Some of them said that they were messengers of Jesus, son of Mary, and that Jesus was the one who sent them to them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “And present to them an example: the companions of the town, when there came to it messengers. When We sent to them two, but they denied them, so We reinforced them with a third.” He said: It was mentioned to us that Jesus, son of Mary, sent two men from the disciples to Antioch, a city in Rome, but they denied them, so He reinforced them with a third. And they said, ‘Indeed, we are messengers to you.’

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said: Sufyan told us, he said: al-Suddi told us, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And present to them an example of the companions of the city. He said: Antioch.

x: Others said: Rather, they were messengers sent to them by God.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us,
m: as far as he was informed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar, and on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: There was in the city of Antioch a Pharaoh from the Pharaohs called Abtahis ibn Abtahis, who worshipped idols and was a polytheist. So God sent the messengers, and they were three: Sadiq, Masdooq, and Sallum. Two of them came to him and to the people of his city, but they denied them. Then God strengthened them with a third. When the messengers summoned him and called him to the command of God, and proclaimed what they had been commanded to do, and criticized his religion and what they were following, he said to them, “Indeed, we see an evil omen in you. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment will surely touch you from us.”

x: God Almighty says: The people of the town said to the three who were sent to them when they informed them that they had been sent to them with what they had been sent with: You, O people, are nothing but people like us. If you were messengers as you say, you would have been angels. And the Most Gracious has not sent down anything. He says: They said: And the Most Gracious has not sent down to you any message or book, nor has He commanded you concerning us anything. You are only lying.

In your saying, Indeed, you have been sent to us. They said, Our Lord knows that we have been sent to you. He says, the messengers said, Our Lord knows that we have been sent to you in what we have called you to, and that we are truthful.

And our duty is only to convey the clear message. He says: Our duty is only to convey to you the message of God with which we were sent to you, conveying it to you clearly, so that we may be able to convey it to you. If you accept it, then you will be granted good fortune, and if you do not accept it, then we have fulfilled what was upon us, and God is the guardian of judgment in it.
God Almighty says: The people of the town said to the messengers: We see bad omens in you. They mean: If you wish us to be afflicted with a calamity, it will be because of you.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “They said: We have bad omens because of you.” They said: Our companions are evil, and it is only because of you. His saying,

, meaning: to its resting place, and this is what was reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The narration mentioned that: Abu Kurayb narrated: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated: Al-A’mash narrated: Ibrahim al-Taimi narrated: his father narrated: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari said: “I was sitting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the mosque. When the sun set, he said: ‘O Abu Dharr, do you know where the sun goes?’ I said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘It goes and prostrates before its Lord, then it asks permission to return and it is given permission, and it is as if it has been told to return from whence you came, and it rises from its place, and that is its resting place.’”
Some of them said about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the sun runs to its resting place
, he said: a single time that it does not exceed.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: It flows according to its course to the extent of its places, meaning: It flows to the furthest of its stations at sunset, then returns and does not go beyond it. They said: That is because it continues to advance every night until it reaches the furthest of its places of setting, then returns. And His statement,
h
That is the decree of the Almighty

, the All-Knowing, means: What we have described of the sun’s course to its resting place is the decree of the Almighty in His vengeance against His enemies, the All-Knowing of the interests of His creation, and other than that of all things, nothing is hidden from Him.
The reciters differed in their reading of His statement,
h
And the moon - We have determined for it phases

Some of the Meccans, some of the Medinans, and some of the Basrans read it as and the moon in the nominative case, in apposition to the sun, since the sun was in apposition to the night. So they followed the sun in the syntax of the moon because it is also one of the signs, just as the night and the day are two signs. So, according to this reading, the interpretation of the statement is: And a sign for them is the moon - We have determined for it phases.

Some of the Meccans, some of the Medinans, some of the Basrans, and most of the Kufan reciters read it as and the moon - We have determined for it meaning: And We have determined for the moon phases, as We did that with the sun. So they traced it back to the ha' of the sun in meaning, because the waw in it is for a delayed verb. What is correct in our view regarding this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. So the interpretation of the statement: And a sign for them is: Our estimation of the moon as phases of decline after its completion, its being full, and its being straight, until it returns like an old cluster. The cluster is from the date palm to the place where the palm branches grow. Rather, God, the Most High, likened it to the old cluster, and the old is the dry, because that of the cluster is hardly ever found except curved and bent when it is old and dry, and it is hardly ever found level and upright, like the branches and twigs of other trees.

So likewise the moon, if it is at the end of the month before its setting, becomes in its curvature and bending similar to that cluster. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, until it returns like an old cluster of dates, meaning: the base of the old cluster.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, until it returns like an old cluster of dates, meaning by the cluster: the dry stalk.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And the moon - We have determined for it phases until it returns [appearing] like an old stalk
, he said: Like a palm branch when it is old and bent.

c: Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi told me: Abu Yazid Al-Kharraz told us,
m: meaning Khalid bin Hayyan Al-Raqi, on the authority of Jaafar bin Barqan, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Asamm, regarding his statement, until it returned like an old cluster of dates, he said: The cluster of the palm tree, when it becomes old, bends.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Isa bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: like an old palm branch, he said: the old palm tree.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said: Ubaid God bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: like an old cluster of dates, he said: the dry cluster.

c: Muhammad bin Omar bin Ali Al-Muqaddami and Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me: Abu Asim Al-Muqaddami told us:
m: I heard Abu Asim say: I heard Sulayman Al-Taymi say regarding his statement, until it returns like an old cluster of dates, he said: the cluster.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Until it returned like an old palm stalk. He said: God determined its stages, so it began to decrease until it was like a palm stalk. He likened it to a palm stalk.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And the moon - We have determined for it phases.
Some of the Meccans, some of the Medinans, and some of the Basrans read it as and the moon in the nominative case, in apposition to the sun, since the sun was in apposition to the night.
So, according to this reading, the interpretation of the statement is: And a sign for them is the moon - We have determined for it phases.

Some of the Meccans, some of the Medinans, some of the Basrans, and most of the Kufan reciters read it as and the moon - We have determined for it meaning: And We have determined for the moon phases, as We did that with the sun.

x: And His statement,
h
Nor can the sun overtake the moon

, God Almighty says: It is not right for the sun to overtake the moon, so that its light is replaced by its light, and all times are day with no night in them. Nor can the night outstrip the day, God Almighty says: Nor can the night outstrip the day, so that its darkness is replaced by its light, and all times are night. And in a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation have said, with differences in their wording in interpreting this, except that the meanings of most of them are what we have said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
It is not for the sun to overtake the moon
, he said: Its light is not like the light of the other, it is not for it to do that.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement,
h
It is not for the sun to overtake the moon
, he said: The light of one of them does not resemble the light of the other, and that is not appropriate for them. And regarding His statement,
h
Nor does the night outstrip the day
, he said: They strive urgently, one of them slipping away from the other.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: h
It is not for the sun to overtake the moon
h
nor does the night outstrip the day
. He said: The light of this one does not overtake the light of that one, nor does that one outstrip the light of that one.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
Nor does the sun overtake the moon
, this is about the light of the moon and the light of the sun. If the sun rises, the moon will have no light, and if the moon rises with its light, the sun will have no light.
h
Nor does the night outstrip the day

, he said: It is in the decree and knowledge of God that the night will not overtake the day until it overtakes it, and its darkness is gone. And it is in the decree of God that the day will not overtake the night until it overtakes it, and its light is gone.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It is not for the sun to overtake the moon

, nor can the night outstrip the day. And for every limit and knowledge they do not exceed nor fall short of. When this authority comes, the authority of that one goes, and when this authority comes, the authority of that one goes.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding this matter: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement,
h
It is not for the sun to overtake the moon
h
nor does the night outstrip the day

, meaning that when they meet in the sky, one of them is in front of the other, and when they set, one of them sets in front of the other. And that from his statement, to overtake, it is in the nominative case with his statement, should. And His saying,
h
And each in an orbit is swimming
, means that everything we mentioned of the sun, the moon, the night, and the day is moving in an orbit. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Abu al-Nu’man al-Hakam ibn Abdullah al-Ajli told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And each, in an orbit, is floating. He said: In an orbit like the orbit of a spindle.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Samad told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Sa’id Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The course of each one of them, meaning the night and the day, is in an orbit, swimming: they move.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And each in an orbit is swimming
: meaning they are swimming in the orbit of the sky.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And each in an orbit is swimming

, rotating, he says: rotating they are Surat Ya-Sin: 40 The sun shall not overtake the moon, nor shall the night outstrip the day. They all, in an orbit, are swimming. swimming: he says: they are running.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And each in an orbit is floating
, meaning: each in an orbit in the heavens.

x: God Almighty says: And as proof for them also, and a sign of Our ability to do whatever We will, We carried their offspring, meaning those of Adam’s children who were saved in Noah’s ship, and by that He, the Most High, meant
h
the laden ark
, and the ark is the ship, and laden means the filled and replenished. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We carried their offspring in the laden ark
, meaning: the full one.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: in
h
the laden ship
means the one that is heavily laden.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us, he said: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id:
h
The laden ark
he said:
m: The loaded one.

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said: Abdul-Warith told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The one who is loaded
, he said: The one who is carried.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
We carried their descendants in the laden ark
, meaning: the ship of Noah, peace be upon him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And a sign for them is that We carried their descendants in the laden ark
, meaning Noah’s ship.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
The laden ark
, he said:
h
The laden ark

is the ship in which Noah was, and the offspring who were in that ship. He said: And the laden is that which has been laden, that which has been placed in it for its people to ride, they put in it what they wanted, so sometimes it was full, and sometimes it was not full.

c: Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabah told us: Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Do you know what a laden ship is? We said: He said: It is the loaded ship.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told us: Harun told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The laden ship
, he said: The loaded one.

x: And His statement:
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride

. God Almighty says: And We created for these polytheists who denied you, O Muhammad, as a favor from Us to them, from the like of that ship in which We carried from the descendants of Adam, those in which We carried those on which they ride from the ships. Then the people of interpretation differed about what was meant by his saying: what they ride.
Some of them said: It is the ships.
Who said that?

c: Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Do you know what
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
means? We said: No. He said: They are the ships that were made after the ship of Noah, similar to it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
, he said: small ships. He said: Ibn Bashar told us, he said:

c: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
, he said: Small ships. Do you not see that he said:
h
And if We will
, We can drown them, and there will be no help for them?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur Ibn Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding this verse,
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
, he said: small ships.

c: Hatim bin Bakr Al-Dhabi told us: Uthman bin Omar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
. He said: Small ships.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
, meaning: the ships that were made after it, meaning after Noah’s ship.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We created for them from the like thereof that which they ride
. He said: They are the ships that are of benefit.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
, he said: And it is this ark.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
, he said: Yes, from the likeness of a ship.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant camels.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that which they ride
means: the camels. God created them as you have seen, so they are the ships of the land, they carry loads on them and ride them.

c: Nasr bin Ali told us: Ghundar told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Ghiyath, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
. He said: Camels.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: Abdullah ibn Shaddad said:
m: h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
meaning camels.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride
, he said: of the livestock.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan said:
m: They are camels. The most similar of the two interpretations of this is the one that says: What is meant by this is ships, and this is because His statement:
h
And if We will

, We can drown them, and they will have no one to help them indicates that this is the case, and this is because it is known that drowning only occurs in water, and there is no drowning on land. Surat Ya-Sin: 42 And We created for them similar things on which they ride.

x: And His statement:
h
And if We will
, We can drown them, but there will be no one to help them. God Almighty says:
h
And if We will
, We can drown these polytheists when they board a ship in the sea. But there will be no one to help them.
There will be no one to help them if We drown them, to rescue them and save them from drowning. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And if We will
, We can drown them, but they will have no helper.
That is, no one to help them. And His statement:
h
Nor will they be saved
means: Nor will anything save them from drowning if We drown them in the sea, unless We save them out of mercy from Us to them, so We save them from it.
And His statement:
h
And provision for a time

means: And We will grant them enjoyment for a term they will reach. So it is as if He said: Nor will they be saved, unless We have mercy on them and grant them enjoyment for a term. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And provision for a time
: meaning until death.

x: God Almighty says: And when it is said to these polytheists who disbelieved in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Beware of what happened before you of God’s punishments and similar punishments to those nations before you who were subjected to it, lest the same happen to you because of your polytheism and your disbelief in His Messenger. “And what will come after you” means: and what will come after your destruction, which you will encounter if you perish in your disbelief. That you may receive mercy means: that your Lord may have mercy upon you if you are wary of that and fear Him by repenting from your polytheism and believing in Him, and adhering to His obedience in what He has enjoined upon you of His obligations. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: And when it is said to them, ‘Fear what is before you,’ means the events of God with the nations who came before them and what will come after them regarding the matter of the Hour. Mujahid used to say about this:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: what is before you he said: what has passed of their sins. This statement is close in meaning to the statement we have mentioned, because its meaning is: Fear the punishment of what is before you of your sins, and what is behind you of the sins that you do and have not yet committed. This is after frightening them with the punishment for their disbelief.

x: And His statement:
h
And there never came to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turned away from it

. God Almighty says: And there never came to these polytheists from Quraysh a sign, meaning a proof from God’s proofs, or a sign from His signs of the truth of His Oneness and the belief in His Messenger, except that they turned away from it, not thinking about it, nor reflecting on it, so that they would know by it what God had used as proof against them.
What is the answer to His statement:
h
And when it is said to them
, ‘Fear what is before you and what is behind you’?
Its answer and the answer to His statement,
h
And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord… His statement

, except that they turn away from it is because their turning away was from every sign of God. So it is sufficient to answer His statement, Fear what is before you and His statement, And no sign comes to them by reporting their turning away from it for that reason, because the meaning of the statement is:
h
And when it is said to them
, ‘Fear what is before you and what is behind you’, they turn away, and when a sign comes to them, they turn away.

God Almighty says: And when it is said to these polytheists, Spend from the provision that God has provided for you, and give from it what God has enjoined upon you for the people of your need and poverty, those who denied the Oneness of God and worshipped others besides Him say to those who believed in God and His Messenger, Should we feed with our wealth and our food those whom God could feed if He willed? And concerning His statement: You are not but in clear error, there are two interpretations: One of them is that it is from what the disbelievers said to the believers, in which case the interpretation of the statement is: You, O people, in what you say to us, Spend from what God has provided for you on your poor, are nothing but straying from the truth and turning away from the right path, clear to whoever reflects and ponders upon it, that they are in error. This is the more correct interpretation of the two interpretations. The other interpretation is that it is from what God said to the polytheists, in which case the interpretation is: You, O disbelievers, in what you say to the believers, Shall we feed those whom God would feed if He willed? are nothing but in clear error, in which case your saying that to them is error.

God Almighty says: And these polytheists who deny God’s threat and the resurrection after death say, hastening their Lord’s punishment, When will this promise come to pass? meaning the promise of the Hour of Resurrection, if you should be truthful, O people. This is what they say to the people of faith in God and His Messenger.

God Almighty says: What these polytheists who hasten God’s threat to them are waiting for is only one blast that will seize them, and that is the blast of terror when the Hour comes. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, and the traces came.
Mention of who said that and what it is from the hadith:

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Auf ibn Abi Jamila told us, on the authority of Abu al-Mughira al-Qawwas, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, who said:
m: “The Trumpet will be blown while the people are in their streets, markets, and gatherings, to the point that a garment will be between two men bargaining, and neither of them will let it go until the Trumpet is blown. And a man will go out from his house and not return until the Trumpet is blown. It is about which God said, ‘
h
They await nothing but a single blast
which will seize them while they are disputing. Then they will not be able to make a will.’”… the verse.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They are awaiting nothing but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “The Hour will strike people while a man is watering his livestock, or repairing his cistern, or displaying his merchandise in the marketplace, or lowering and raising his scales. It will strike them likewise, and they will not be able to make any wills or return to their families.”

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
They await nothing but a single blast

, he said: The blast is a single blast. Abu Kurayb narrated: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharbi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’, on the authority of someone who mentioned him, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the trumpet and gave it to Israfil. He is placing it on his mouth, staring at the Throne, waiting for the command to be given. Abu Hurayrah said: O Messenger of God, what is the trumpet? He said: A horn. He said: How is it? He said: A great horn in which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of the stun, and the third is the blast of the resurrection for the Lord of the Worlds. God will command Israfil with the first blast, and he will say: Blow the blast of terror. The inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth will be terrified, except for whom God wills. God will command him to continue it and prolong it, and he will not cease. It is the one about which God says: ‘These people will not wait except for a single blast which will have no stopping.’ Then God will command Israfil with the blast of the stun, and he will say: “He will blow the blast of the Thunderbolt, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth will be weakened, except for whom God wills. Then they will be extinguished. Then He will cause to die whoever remains. Then, when nothing remains but God, the One, the Eternal Refuge, He will replace the earth with another and the heavens. He will spread it out and level it, and extend it like the extension of a rough hide. You will see therein neither crookedness nor unevenness. Then God will rebuke the creation with a rebuke, and at once they will be in this replaced place, in the same places as the first. What was in its belly will be in its belly, and what was on its back will be on its back.” The reciters differed in their reading of His statement:
h

From a Merciful Lord
, means: Merciful to them, as He did not punish them for their past crimes in this world.

x: By his saying and they distinguished themselves he means: they distinguished themselves, and it is an ifta'alu, from maza yamiz, a verb from which he yamtaza yamtazaan. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And separate yourselves today
, O criminals, he said: separate yourself from all good.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharbi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’, on the authority of someone who narrated to him, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will command Hell, and a bright, dark neck will emerge from it. Then He will say: ‘Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? ’… the verse, until His saying: ‘This is Hell which you were promised. ’ ‘
h
And separate yourselves today

, O criminals. ’ So the people will separate themselves and kneel, and this is the saying of God: ‘And every nation will see… the verse.” The interpretation of the statement then is: And distinguish yourselves from the believers today, O you who disbelieve in God, for you will come to a place other than their place of arrival, and you will enter a place other than their entrance.

x: And His statement,
h
Did I not enjoin upon you

, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - indeed, he is to you a clear enemy, and in the speech there is an omitted element that is sufficient because of the speech’s indication of it, which is: Then it is said,
h
Did I not enjoin upon you

, O children of Adam, meaning: Did I not command you and order you in this world not to worship Satan, so that you would obey him in disobeying God, indeed, he is to you a clear enemy, meaning: And I say to you: Satan is to you a clear enemy, he has made his enmity clear to you by refusing to prostrate to your father Adam, out of envy of him, for the honor that God had given him, and his deception of him, until he expelled him and his wife from Paradise.
And His statement, “
h
And worship Me

. This is a straight path.” He says: Did I not command you to worship Me alone, and not all other gods and rivals besides Me, and to obey Me alone? For sincerity in worshipping Me, obedience to Me alone, and disobedience to Satan, is the true religion and the straight path.

God Almighty means by His saying, And he has certainly led astray many of you: Satan has indeed turned many of you away from obeying Me and singling Me out as God until they worshipped him and took other gods besides Me to worship.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And indeed, He has led astray a mountain among you, he said: a creation. The reciters differed in the recitation of this word. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufians recited it as jabalan with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam.

x: Some of the Meccans and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as jabalan with a damma on the jim and the ba’ and a soft lam.

Some of the reciters of Basra recited it as jabalan with a damma on the jim and a sukoon on the ba’. All of these are well-known dialects. However, I do not like to recite it except with one of the two recitations: one of them is with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam, and the other is a damma on the jim and the ba’ and a soft lam, because that is the recitation followed by the majority of the reciters of the regions. And His statement,
h
Did you not understand
? means:
h
Did you not understand
, O polytheists, when you obeyed Satan in worshipping other than God, that it is not appropriate for you to obey your enemy and the enemy of God, and worship other than God.

However, I do not like to recite it except with one of the two recitations: one of them is with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam, and the other is a damma on the jim and the ba’ and a soft lam, because that is the recitation followed by the majority of the reciters of the regions.

x: And His statement,
h
This is Hell which you were promised
, means:
h
This is Hell which you were promised
in this world because of your disbelief in God and your denial of His messengers, so you used to deny it. It was said that Hell is the first gate of the gates of Hell.
And His statement,
h
Burn in it today for what you used to disbelieve
, means: burn in it today and return it, meaning today: the Day of Resurrection. For what you used to disbelieve, means: for what you used to deny in this world and lie about it.
God Almighty means by His statement,
h
This Day We shall seal up their mouths

, that is, This Day We shall seal the mouths of the polytheists, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. “And their hands will speak to Us” about what they did in this world of sins against God. And their feet will bear witness it was said that what speaks from their feet is their thighs on the left foot. What they used to earn in this world of sins. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Yunus ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Humayd ibn Hilal: Abu Burdah said:
m: Abu Musa said: “The believer will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection, and his Lord will present to him his deeds between him and Him. He will confess and say: ‘Yes, O Lord, I have done, I have done.’ God will forgive him his sins and conceal them from him. There is no creature on earth that can see any of those sins and make his good deeds apparent, and he will wish that all people could see them. The disbeliever and the hypocrite will be called to account, and his deeds and knowledge will be presented to him, and he will deny them and say: ‘O Lord, by Your glory, this angel has decreed for me something that I did not do.’ The angel will say to him: ‘Did you not do such and such on such and such a day in such and such a place?’ He will say: ‘No, by Your glory, O Lord, I did not do it.’ When he does that, his mouth will be sealed. Al-Ash’ari said: ‘I think the first part of it to speak will be his right thigh.’ Then he recited: ‘This Day We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.’”

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: It will be said to a man on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:You did such and such. He will say: I did not do it. Then his mouth will be sealed and his limbs will speak, and he will say to his limbs: May God distance you. I only disputed about you.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Today We will seal their mouths
... the verse. He said: There had been disputes and talk, but this was the end of it, and He sealed their mouths.

c: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta’i told me: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Damdam ibn Zur’ah, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir,
m: that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The first thing of a person to speak on the Day when God seals the mouths will be his left thigh.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement,
h
And if We willed
, We could have blinded their eyes and they would have raced along the path.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is:
h
And if We willed
, We could have blinded them to guidance and led them astray from the straight path.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And if We willed
, We could have blinded their eyes, meaning: I would have led them astray and blinded them to guidance.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: If We had willed, We would have left them blind.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement, “
h
And if We willed
, We could have blinded their eyes and they would race along the path. How could they see?” He said: If He willed, He could have blinded their eyes and left them blind, wandering about.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God, “
h
And if We willed

, We could have obliterated their eyes and they would race along the path. But how could they see?” He says: If We willed, We could have left them blind and wandering. This statement that we mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatada is more similar to the interpretation of the speech, because God only threatens a disbelieving people with it, so there is no basis for saying while they are disbelievers: If We willed, We could have led them astray, and He has led them astray. Rather, He said: If We willed, We could have punished them for their disbelief, so We obliterated their eyes and made them blind, so that they cannot see the path, nor can they be guided to it. Obliterating the eye means that there is no gap between the eyelids, and that is the slit between the eyelids, just as the wind obliterates a trace. It is said, a blind, obliterated, and obliterated person. His saying,
h
So race to the path
, means: So hasten to take the path.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
So race to the path
, he said, the road.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So race to the path
: meaning the road.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
So race to the path
, he said: The path is the road. And His saying,
h
How can they see
? means, What path can they see to take, when We have blinded their eyes?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
How can they see
? when We have blinded their eyes. Those who interpreted His statement,
h
And if We willed
, We could have blinded their eyes, to mean blindness to guidance said: The interpretation of His statement, How then can they see? is: How then can they be guided to the truth?

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Sal told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
How can they see
? He said: How can they be guided?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
How can they see
? He said: They do not see the truth.

x: And His statement,
h
And if We willed
, We could have transformed them into their places. God Almighty says:
h
And if We willed

, We could have made these polytheists sit on their feet in their homes. So they would not have been able to go forward, nor would they have returned. He says: They would not have been able to go forward, nor to return behind them. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said something similar to what we have said about it.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: h
And if We willed
, We could have transformed them into their places. He said: If We willed, We could have made them sit down.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if We willed

, We could have transformed them into their places: meaning, We could have made them sit on their feet. So they would not have been able to go forward or return: so they would not have been able to advance or fall back.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If We had willed, We could have destroyed them in their homes.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And if We willed
, We could have transformed them into their places, so they would not have been able to proceed nor return. He said,
h
And if We willed
, We could have destroyed them in their dwellings. Place and location have the same meaning. We have already explained that previously.

x: God Almighty says,
h
And whomsoever We grant long life

, so that we extend his life, We reverse him in creation, so that we return him to the state he was in youth, of decrepitude and old age. This is the reversal in creation, so he no longer knows anything after the knowledge he had. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And whomsoever We grant long life

, We reverse him in creation. We say: Whoever We extend in life, We reverse him in creation, so that he does not know anything after knowing, meaning old age. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement nankasahu We will turn it upside down. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians recited it as nankasahu with a fatha on the first nun and a sukun on the second. The majority of the Kufic reciters recited it as nankasahu with a damma on the first nun, a fatha on the second, and a shaddah on the kaf. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one the reciter recites is correct. However, the one that most of the Kufi reciters follow is more pleasing to me, because God’s reversal of creation is only one state after another, one thing after another, so that supports the emphasis. They also differed in the reading of His statement,
h
Do they not then understand

? The readers of Medina read it, Afala ta'qaloon with a ta' as an address. The readers of Kufa read it with a ya' as a narration. Reading that with a ya' is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation, because it is an argument from God against the polytheists about whom He said, And if We willed,
h
We could have obliterated their eyes
. So making that a narration in the same way as making His statement,
h
We could have obliterated their eyes

, is more pleasing to me, even though the other part is not supported. God Almighty means by His statement, Do they not reason?: Do these polytheists not understand God’s ability to do whatever He wills by witnessing what they witness of His disposition of His creation as He wills and loves, from smallness to old age, and from being turned upside down after old age into decrepitude?
