The majority of the Kufic reciters recited it as nankasahu with a damma on the first nun, a fatha on the second, and a shaddah on the kaf.
The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one the reciter recites is correct.

However, the one that most of the Kufi reciters follow is more pleasing to me, because God’s reversal of creation is only one state after another, one thing after another, so that supports the emphasis.
They also differed in the reading of His statement, Do they not then understand?
The readers of Medina read it, Afala ta'qaloon with a ta' as an address.
The readers of Kufa read it with a ya' as a narration.

x: And His statement,
h
And We did not teach him poetry
, nor is it befitting for him, God Almighty says: We did not teach Muhammad poetry, nor is it befitting for him to be a poet.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We did not teach him poetry

, nor is it befitting for it. He said: It was said to Aisha: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite any poetry? She said: It was the most hated speech to him, except that he would recite the verse of the brother of Banu Qais, making its end its beginning, and its beginning its end. Abu Bakr said to him: It is not like this. The Prophet of God said: By God, I am not a poet, nor is it befitting for me. And His statement,
h
It is only a reminder
, God Almighty says:
h
It is only a reminder
, meaning by His statement, “
h
It is only a reminder

to you, O people, God reminded you of Him by sending him to you and bestowing him upon you according to your portion. “And a clear Qur’an,” meaning: And this which Muhammad brought to you is a clear Qur’an, meaning: It makes clear to whoever contemplates it with reason and understanding that it is a revelation from God that He sent down to Muhammad, and that it is not poetry or the rhyme of a soothsayer.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And a clear Qur’an, he said: This is the Qur’an.

evidence.text: She said: It was the most hated speech to him, except that he would recite the verse of the brother of Banu Qais, making its end its beginning, and its beginning its end.

x: And his saying,
h
To warn whoever is alive

, means: Muhammad was only mentioned to you to warn whoever among you, O people, is alive in heart, who understands what is said to him, and comprehends what is explained to him, and is not dead-hearted and dull. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
To warn whoever is alive
, he said: Whoever is rational.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
To warn whoever is alive
: alive in heart, alive in sight. His statement,
h
And the word will come true against the disbelievers

, means: And the punishment will come true against the people who disbelieve in God, who turn away from following Him, and who turn away from what He has brought them from God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the word will come into effect against the disbelievers based on their deeds.

x: God Almighty says, Have they not seen, these polytheists who associate others with God, the gods and idols, that We have created for them from what Our hands have made? He says: from what We have created of creation, livestock, which are the livestock that God created for the children of Adam, and made subservient to them from camels, cows, and sheep. They own them, He says: They dispose of them as they wish, by their control and control over them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, and they are its owners: meaning they are in control.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made

, grazing livestock, so they own them? It was said to him: Are they camels? He said: Yes. He said: Cows are among the grazing livestock, but they are not included in this verse. He said: Camels, cows, and sheep are among the grazing livestock, and he recited eight pairs (Al-Anʿam 6:143, Az-Zumar 39:6). He said: Cows and camels are the grazing livestock, but sheep are not included in the grazing livestock.

x: And His statement, And We have subjected them to them, means: We have subjected these livestock to them. And some of them they ride, means: Some of them they ride, such as camels that they travel on. It is said: This is a riding animal, and riding with the dammah is the action. And some of them they eat their meat. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We have made them subservient to them, and some of them they ride: they ride them and travel on them, and some of them they eat their meat.

x: God Almighty says: And they have benefits from these livestock, and that is the benefit in their wool, fur, and hair, by making them furniture and provisions, and from their skins, shelters, and drinking places from which they drink their milk.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they have therein benefits they wear its wool and drinks they drink its milk. And His saying,
h
Will they not then be grateful
? means:
h
Will they not then be grateful
for this blessing of mine, and my kindness to them through my obedience, and singling out divinity and worship for me, and abandoning the obedience of Satan and the worship of idols?

x: His statement,
h
And they have taken gods besides God
, means: These polytheists have taken gods besides God that they worship, so that they may be aided, meaning: hoping that those gods will aid them from God’s punishment and torment.

God Almighty says: These gods cannot help them against God if He intends evil for them, nor can they ward off harm from them. And His saying, And they are a prepared army for them, means: And these polytheists are a prepared army for their gods. The commentators differed in their interpretation of His statement, presented, and where they will be present with them.
Some of them said: What he meant by that is: They are an army present with them at the reckoning.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, And they will be a host prepared for them, he said: at the reckoning. Akhoon said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They are an army prepared for them in this world, and they become angry on their behalf.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They cannot help them the gods and they are a ready army for them and the polytheists get angry for the sake of the gods in this world, but they do not bring them good, nor do they ward off evil from them, they are only idols. What Qatada said is the more correct of the two opinions in our view regarding the interpretation of that, because when the polytheists are brought to account, the idols and what they used to worship will disown them, so how can they be their soldiers at that time? But in this world they have soldiers who become angry on their behalf and fight for them.

x: And His Almighty’s saying, So let not their statement grieve you, means that the Almighty is saying to His Prophet Muhammad: “So let not the statement of these polytheists among your people that you are a poet, and what you have brought us is poetry, grieve you, O Muhammad, and that they deny the signs of God and reject your prophethood. And His saying, “Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare,” means that the Almighty is saying: We know that what is calling them to that statement is envy, and they know that what you have brought them is not poetry, nor does it resemble poetry, and that you are not a liar. So We know what they conceal of their knowledge of the truth of what you are calling them to, and what they declare of their denial of it openly with their tongues.
God Almighty says:
h
Does man not see
that We created him? There is a difference of opinion about the man meant by His statement
h
Does man not see
Some of them said: It refers to Abi bin Khalaf.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed
? He said: Abu bin Khalaf brought a bone to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And He has given us an example, is Abi ibn Khalaf.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, He said, ‘Who will bring the bones to life when they have decayed?’ It was mentioned to us that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a rotten bone, crumbled it, then scattered it in the wind, then said: O Muhammad, who will bring this to life when it has decayed? He said: God will bring it to life, then cause it to die, then cause you to enter the Fire. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught him this on the Day of Uhud.”

x: Others said: Rather, he meant Al-Aas bin Wael Al-Sahmi.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Abu Bishr told us on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: “Al-Aas ibn Wa’il as-Sahmi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a decayed bone. He crumbled it in front of him and said: ‘O Muhammad, will God raise this up to life after it has decayed?’ He said: ‘Yes, God will raise this up, then cause you to die, then bring you back to life, then cause you to enter the fire of Hell.’ He said: Then the verses were revealed: ‘
h
Does man not see
that We created him from a sperm-drop? Then at once he is a clear adversary.’ … to the end of the verse.”

x: Others said: Rather, he meant Abdullah bin Ubayy.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
Does man not see

that We created him from a sperm-drop… until the words while it was disintegrated. He said: “Abdullah ibn Ubayy came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a decayed bone and broke it with his hand, then said: O Muhammad, how can God resurrect this when it has disintegrated? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will resurrect this, and cause you to die, then cause you to enter Hell. God said: ‘Say: He will give it life who produced it the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation.’” So the interpretation of the statement is: Has not this man seen who says:
h
Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed

? “We created him from a sperm-drop and proportioned him with a well-proportioned creation?” Then he will be an opponent. He says: Then he will be an opponent to his Lord, arguing with Him about what his Lord told him I will do. This is God informing him that He will revive His creation after their death, so he says: Who will give life to these bones when they have decayed? denying God’s ability to revive them. His saying, clear, means: He makes clear to whoever hears his argument and what he says that he is arguing with his Lord who created him.

x: And His statement,
h
And he has set forth for us an example and has forgotten his own creation
, meaning: And He has set forth for us an example by His statement,
h
Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed

? since no one is able to give life to that, meaning: So We made him like one who is not able to give life to that of creation. And has forgotten his creation, meaning: And He has forgotten how We created him, and that he was nothing but a sperm-drop, so We made him a sound, speaking creation, meaning: So he did not think about His creation, so it is known that the One who created him from a sperm-drop until he became a sound, speaking, and acting human being is not unable to bring the dead back to life, and the decayed bones back to humans as they were before they perished.

God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to this polytheist who says to you: Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed? He will give them life who produced them the first time meaning: He will give them life who originated them the first time when they were nothing. And He is Knowing of all creation meaning: He is All-Knowing of all His creation: how He causes death, how He brings life, how He refrains from starting, and how He restores. Nothing of His creation is hidden from Him.

God Almighty says: Say, He will give life to it who produced it the first time. “Who made for you from the green tree fire.” He says: He who brought forth for you from the green tree fire that burns the tree, is not prevented from doing what He wants, nor is He unable to revive the bones that have been thrown away, and return them to normal human beings, and a new creation, as He created them the first time. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Who made for you fire from the green tree, meaning: The One who brought out this fire from this tree is able to resurrect it. His saying, Then you kindle from it. He says: Then you kindle from the tree. He said, from it, and the ha is from the mention of the tree, and he did not say: from it. The tree is the plural of tree, because it emerged like the emergence of fruit and pebbles. If it had been said: from it, it would have been correct as well, because the Arabs mention something like this and feminize it.

x: And His statement,
h
Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them

? God Almighty says, alerting this disbeliever who said, Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed? to the error of his statement and the enormity of his ignorance, Is not He who created the seven heavens and the earth able to create the likes of you? For creating the likes of you from decayed bones is not greater than creating the heavens and the earth. He says: So if it is not impossible for Him to create what is greater than your creation, then how can it be impossible for Him to bring bones to life after they have decayed and worn out? And His statement, Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing, He says: Yes, He is able to create the likes of them, and He is the Creator of whatever He wills, the Doer of whatever He desires, the Knower of everything that He has created and will create, and nothing is hidden from Him.
God Almighty says: His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.
Qatada said about that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. He said: This is a parable. His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, Be, and it is. He said: There is nothing in the speech of the Arabs that is lighter or easier than that, so God’s command is like that.

x: And His statement,
h
So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion over all things
, meaning, the Most High, the Majestic, says: So glorify He in whose hand is the dominion over all things and their treasuries. And His statement,
h
And to Him you will be returned
, meaning:
h
And to Him you will be returned
and will be destined after your death.
